answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x under daily settlement peak with heavy writes, so saturation is the load-aligned hypothesis and add_capacity is the intervention that can restore availability without shedding customer writes. Circuit breaking is rejected because failing fast would drop writes. Rollback is a real alternate (release shipped 2h ago; climb began 90m ago) but memory_b1 addressed an error spike, not latency, and a mistaken rollback would spend the only window. memory_b5 recovered write latency by offloading report reads, which are not in evidence. memory_b3 is the closest precedent but describes headroom provisioned before a peak, so it may not transfer to mid-peak add; verifying that archive before commit. Uncertainty on release-vs-load cause is retained.
